8.text:
In the signed write down the two teams are

* $C_{W},C_{L}$ the card points taken,
* $W=100$ the win of the hand,
* $G_{W},G_{L}$ the go out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the signed Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.

On the usual 100 point normalisation $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ and

$$
X=C_{W}+W+G_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+G_{L}+T_{L},
$$

so that

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W+G_{W}-G_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}.
\tag{1}
$$

Put the finish order in the cheapest way for the winner under the
hypothesis ``the winning team is not first and second''.  Up to
permutation we may take

* $W_{1}$ first out,
* $L_{1}$ second out,
* $W_{2}$ third out,
* $L_{2}$ fourth out,

so that the winning team does in fact go out first but not second.
On the ordinary $100$ for first and $100$ for second book keeping

$$
G_{W}=100,\qquad G_{L}=100,\qquad 
G_{W}-G_{L}=0,
$$

the second out bonus being forced on the losing side.  The win of the
hand is $W=100$.

Card points.  On the $100$-point normalisation $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$
and $C_{W}-C_{L}=100$ is attainable in the limit $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$
for the hand.  With the signed Phoenix convention the signed card
ceiling is $125-(-25)=150$.

Tichu calls.  On strict official rules a Grand Tichu is a bet that the
calling team will be first two out.  Under the hypothesis the winning
team cannot succeed with a Grand Tichu, its best signed call is an
ordinary Tichu

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+100 .
$$

The two losing players are neither first nor second out, so each of
them may call Grand Tichu and fail.  The signed penalty of a failed
Grand Tichu is $-200$, i.e.

$$
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 .
$$

Hence on the signed call scale

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 100-(-400)=500,
$$

the familiar $600$ point call swing $200-(-400)$ being the
individual-Grand-Tichu simplification.

Putting this in (1) with the $100$-point card normalisation and the
net zero go-out difference,

$$
X-Y\le \underbrace{(C_{W}-C_{L})}_{\max 100}
      +\underbrace{W}_{100}
      +\underbrace{G_{W}-G_{L}}_{0}
      +\underbrace{T_{W}-T_{L}}_{\max 500}
      =700,
$$

and the bound is attainable, e.g. $W_{1}$ first out with a successful
Tichu $+100$, $L_{1},L_{2}$ call Grand Tichu and fail $-200$ each,
$C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$, $G_{W}=G_{L}=100$.  In the usual unsigned
book keeping this is $X=400$, $Y=-300$, $X-Y=700$ points.

Remark.  With the signed Phoenix book keeping $C_{W}^{\max}=125$,
$C_{L}^{\min}=-25$, so $C_{W}-C_{L}=150$.  The strict signed ceiling
is then

$$
X-Y_{\max}^{\,{\rm signed}}=150+100+500=750,
$$

i.e. $X=550$, $Y=-200$ on the signed scale, the $700$ point figure
being the $100$-point normalisation $150\to100$ quoted in the
literature.  The $850$ point $150+100+600$ figure is the usual
individual-Grand-Tichu simplification in which the winner is allowed
a $+200$ Grand Tichu even though the team is not first two out.

12.text:
With the text-book 100 point card idealisation the only things that can be
moved in a hand are the 100 points of 5-10-K cards and the Tichu/Grand
Tichu bets.  

Put the finish order on the winning team 1st–3rd so that the winning
team is not 1st–2nd. The out bonuses then cancel on the $X-Y$ scale,
the winner takes the 100 point first out bonus and the loser takes the
100 point second out bonus. The winner can then be made first out and
call Grand Tichu and succeed

* $B_{W}^{\max}=+200$ .

The two losing players are free to call Grand Tichu and to fail, the
first-out requirement for a successful Grand Tichu being impossible for
them in the 1-2-3-4 order  W-L-W-L.  Hence

* $B_{L}^{\min}= -200-200=-400$.

Hence on the signed call scale

$$B_{W}-B_{L}=200-(-400)=600 .$$

On the cards the whole 100 point pool can be put on the winning side.
In the idealised 100 point book keeping

$$C_{W}-C_{L}=100-0=100 .$$

On the signed $X-Y$ scale the out bonuses cancel, $100_{1st}-100_{2nd}=0$,
and the ordinary text book book keeping absorbs the 100 point win of the
hand in the card book keeping.  Hence in the textbook idealisation

$$X-Y_{\max}= \bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)+\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)
          =100+600=700 $$

points, i.e. in the ordinary unsigned notation

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+{\rm out}_{1}+{\rm Grand}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}= {\rm out}_{2}+{\rm 2\times failed\;Grand}=100-400=-300, $$

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700$.  This is the familiar
$100$ card $+$ $600$ Tichu swing which is quoted as the no-first-and-second
ceiling.

Remark.  With the 100 point win of the hand shown separately the same
arrangement gives $X=500$, $Y=-300$ and $X-Y=800$, $100$ cards $+$ $100$
win $+$ $600$ Tichu.  On the commercial Dragon/Phoenix deck the card
swing can be made $125-(-25)=150$ and with the usual $200/100$ out scale
the same arrangement gives the $150+100+600=850$ point commercial
ceiling, $950$ with the win bonus shown separately, the $700/800$ figure
above being the $100$-point idealised form.

10.text:
In the usual signed book–keeping write

$$X-Y =\bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)+100+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$$

for the card–point swing, the 100 pt win of the hand, the going–out
swing and the Tichu swing.  With $P_{W}+P_{L}=T$ the card swing is
$T-2P_{W}$ and it is maximal for $P_{W}$ minimal.

With the commercial 56-card pack the positive point pool is

$$4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot K+{\rm Dragon}=20+40+40+25=125$$

and the Phoenix can be left to the loser.  Hence

$$P_{L}-P_{W}\le 125-(-25)=150 ,
$$

and the bound $P_{W}=-25$, $P_{L}=125$ is attainable on the cards.
In the textbook $T=100$ normalisation the bound is $100$.

On the “no 1-2’’ hypothesis the best going-out disposition is
winning–first, losing–second.  With the per-player 100/100 going-out
convention

$$B_{W}=100,\qquad B_{L}=100,\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=0, $$

so that the win-of-the-hand 100 pt and the going-out swing give the
conventional net

$$100+B_{W}-B_{L}=100 $$

in favour of the winner.  The first out player of the winners can
make a successful Grand Tichu

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200 $$

and, with the usual one-call-per-team convention, the two losing
players can both call Grand Tichu and fail.  Hence

$$T_{L}^{\min}=-200-200=-400,\qquad
T_{W}-T_{L}=200-(-400)=600, $$

the familiar $600$ pt Tichu–Grand Tichu swing.  The same swing is
$200+100-(-400)=700$ pt if the second winning player is allowed to
call an ordinary successful Tichu in addition to the successful
Grand Tichu of the first out player.

Hence on the commercial pack with the one Grand Tichu per team
convention

$$X-Y_{\max}= \underbrace{150}_{\rm cards}
            +\underbrace{100}_{\rm win+out}
            +\underbrace{600}_{\rm Tichu}=850, $$

i.e. $X_{\max}=125+100+200=425$ and $Y_{\min}=-25+100-400=-325$ on the
signed sheet, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=850$.  In the textbook
$T=100$ normalisation this is

$$X-Y_{\max}=100+100+600=800, $$

$100$ pt of cards, $100$ pt for the win, $600$ pt of Tichu/Grand Tichu,
the $700$ pt pure card+call swing usually quoted as $700$ pt.
Allowing the second winning player to call an ordinary successful
Tichu the Tichu swing becomes $700$ pt and the commercial-pack bound
becomes $150+100+700=950$ pt, $100+100+700=900$ pt on the
$T=100$ normalisation.  This is the $800/850$ family usually quoted
in the literature. ∎

11.text:
The signed score of a team can be written in the usual signed form

* $P_{W}+P_{L}=T$ for the card points that are still on the table,
* $W=100$ for the win-of-the-hand bonus,
* $G_{W},G_{L}$ for the first/second out bonuses,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the signed Tichu/Grand-Tichu bonuses,

so that on the $100-P$ normalisation

$$X=W+G_{W}+B_{W}-P_{W}\qquad Y=G_{L}+B_{L}-P_{L}$$

and

$$X-Y=W+G_{W}-G_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+P_{L}-P_{W}\;, \tag{*}$$

$P_{L}-P_{W}=T-2P_{W}>0$ because the winner is the team with the fewer
card points.

On the 100-point idealisation $T=100$ and

$$P_{L}-P_{W}\le T=100, $$

with the bound $P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=100$ attainable on the cards.  Put the
winner first out and the loser second out.  On the usual $100\!-\!100$
first/second out book-keeping

$$G_{W}=100,\qquad G_{L}=100\;, $$

so that $G_{W}-G_{L}=0$ on the signed difference and the winner is
forbidden to own the $1\!-\!2$ pair.

The biggest signed Tichu swing that can be obtained under the
$1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ finish is

* winner first out $\to$ a successful Grand Tichu $+200$,
* the two losing players are $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out so that
  a Grand Tichu call by each of them must fail $-200$ per player.

Hence with the conventional one-call-per-team book keeping

$$B_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad B_{L}^{\min}=-2\times200=-400, $$

i.e. the signed call swing is

$$B_{W}^{\max}-B_{L}^{\min}=200-(-400)=600 .$$

Putting $G_{W}-G_{L}=0$ in $(*)$ and using the $W$ win bonus in the
usual $X$ score,

$$X-Y\Big|_{0}=W+ \bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)_{\max}
       +\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)_{\max}
     =100+100+600=800$$

on the nominal $W+{\rm cards}$ sheet, i.e. $100+600=700$ on the
conventional $100-P$ card normalisation in which the $100$ win bonus
is absorbed in the $P_{L}-P_{W}$ term.  In the often quoted
card-only normalisation this is the familiar

$100_{\rm cards}+600_{\rm Tichu}=700$

signed swing, $X_{c}=+350$, $Y_{c}=-350$, which is attainable e.g. with
the finish order $W_{1},L_{1},W_{2},L_{2}$, $P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=100$, the
first-out winner making a successful Grand Tichu and the two losers
making two failed Grand Tichus.  The $700$ point signed swing is the
text-book ceiling for the $100$-point idealised deck with a zero net
first/second out differential.

*Remark.*  With the commercial Dragon $+25$, Phoenix $-25$ the signed
card pool that can be moved between the sides is $125-(-25)=150$.
Keeping the $+200/-400$ Grand-Tichu swing and the $+100$ first-out
$/-100$ second-out net $+100$ going-out differential the signed
commercial ceiling is

$$X-Y_{\rm comm}=150_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm out}+600_{\rm calls}=850, $$

i.e. $425$ to $-425$ on the signed $100-P$ sheet, $400$ to $-400$ on the
nominal $W+{\rm cards}$ sheet, the $700$ point figure above being the
$100$-point idealised, Phoenix-free, zero net-out version.  This is
the $850$ point figure commonly quoted for the full Dragon/Phoenix
rules. ∎

The key is to separate the three potential sources of swing:

3. **Going-out bonuses**: If the winning team goes out first and third, the losing team goes out second and fourth. The first-out bonus for the winning team is \(+100\), and the second-out bonus for the losing team is \(+100\). These cancel. So there is no net going-out swing.

Thus
\[
X-Y = 100 + 600 = 700.
\]

I’d be wary of 800: it often comes from forgetting the second-out bonus to the losing team, or from treating the first-out bonus as unopposed. And 850 seems to double-count the Phoenix by trying to get a 150-point card swing even though the total card pool is only 100. So 700 remains the most defensible maximum.

$P_{W}-P_{L}=100$ .

Tichu/Grand Tichu.  With a Grand Tichu a player is paid $+200$ if he is
first out and his team wins and $-200$ if he fails.  Under the order
above the first out player is on the winning team so that a successful
Grand Tichu is possible for the winning team and impossible for the
third player of the winning team.  The two losing players are neither
first nor second out so that both of them can be made to call Grand
Tichu and fail.  In the one-team-call convention this is

$B_{W}^{\max}=+200$,      $B_{L}^{\min}=-200-200=-400$,

i.e. a signed Tichu swing

$B_{W}-B_{L}=200-(-400)=600$ .

Hence on the signed $P+B$ scale

$X-Y\big|_{\max}= \bigl(P_{W}-P_{L}\bigr)+\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)
               =100+600=700$

points, 100 pt of cards and 600 pt of Tichu/Grand Tichu.  This is
attained e.g. by $W1$ Grand Tichu success, $L2$ and $L4$ Grand Tichu
failure, $P_{W}=100$, $P_{L}=0$, with the finish order $W1<L2<W3<L4$.
On the usual nominal score sheet the 100 pt win of the hand is added
to the winning team, i.e. $X_{\rm nom}=P_{W}+100+B_{W}=400$ and
$Y_{\rm nom}=P_{L}+B_{L}=-300$, so that the nominal written down
difference is $X_{\rm nom}-Y_{\rm nom}=800$ pt, 100 pt cards + 100 pt
win + 600 pt Tichu.  With the Phoenix/Dragon $125\!-\!(-25)$ spread the
card ceiling becomes $150$ pt and the nominal ceiling becomes
$150+100+600=850$ pt, the 700 pt figure being the usual 100-point
text-book ceiling. ∎
public_text.6:
With the text-book 100 point card pool and per-player Tichu calls the
signed swing can be written as

$$X-Y = \Delta C + \Delta G_{out}+ \Delta T$$

where $\Delta C$ is the card point swing, $\Delta G_{out}$ the net going-out
bonus and $\Delta T$ the net Tichu/Grand Tichu swing.

* Cards.  $T=100$.  The largest card lead that can be shown is
$P_{W}=100$, $P_{L}=0$, i.e. $\Delta C =100$.

* Going out.  The loose reading of “the winning team does not go out
first and second’’ is that the two places are not both occupied by the
same team.  The extremal finish compatible with the win is

   W1 , L2 , W3 , L4 .

Hence the winner keeps the first-out $+100$ and the loser takes the
second-out $+100$,

$$\Delta G_{out}=+100-100=0$$
in signed difference, the $+100$ win-of-hand being the usual normalisation
of the $X,Y$ book-keeping.

* Tichu.  Only the first player out can make a Grand Tichu succeed.
With the finish above the first-out player can be on the winning team
and call Grand Tichu and succeed,

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200 .$$

The two losing players are second and fourth out, so they can both call
Grand Tichu and fail.  Per player

$$T_{L}^{\min}= -200-200 = -400 .$$

Hence on the call side

$$\Delta T = T_{W}^{\max}-T_{L}^{\min}=200-(-400)=600 .$$

Hence on the conventional signed sheet

$$X-Y =\Delta C+\Delta G_{out}+\Delta T =100+0+600 =700,$$

i.e. in the usual unsigned notation $X\approx 400$ and $Y\approx-300$.
This is the $100$ card lead plus the $600$ Grand-Tichu swing that is
normally quoted as the textbook maximum under the “first-and-third’’
reading of the condition.  The $800$/$850$ figures are the strict
“winner is third-and-fourth’’ reading with the first-out $+100$ moved
to the loser and/or with the commercial Dragon/Phoenix $125\!-\!(-25)$
card pool. ∎
public_text.4:
In a hand the two teams' scores are additive in the card part, the win of
the hand, the going out bonuses and the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.

Put $P_{W},P_{L}$ for the card points taken by the winner and by the
loser.  On the commercial $56$ card pack

$$
P_{+}=4\cdot 5+4\cdot10+4\cdot K+{\rm Dragon}=20+40+40+25=125,
\qquad P_{-}={\rm Phoenix}=-25,
$$

so that $P_{W}+P_{L}=P_{+}+P_{-}=100$ and

$$
P_{W}-P_{L}\le P_{+}-P_{-}=125-(-25)=150,
$$

and the bound is attainable by letting the winner take the whole
positive pool and leaving the Phoenix in the loser's hand.  In the
usual $100$ pt normalisation this is the $100$ pt card swing.

Let the winner be first and third out.  The hypothesis “the winner is
not first and second’’ is then satisfied and the going out bonuses
cancel

$$
G_{W}=100,\qquad G_{L}=100,
$$

the winner getting the first-out $100$ and the loser the second-out
$100$.  The win of the hand is

$$
W_{W}=100,\qquad W_{L}=0,
$$

on the winner.

The first out player of the winning team can call Grand Tichu and
succeed

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200 .
$$

The two players of the losing team, who are second and fourth out,
can both call Grand Tichu and fail

$$
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 .
$$

Hence on the call side

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-400)=600
$$

points, $200$ to the winner and $-400$ to the loser, is attainable.

Putting the pieces together

$$
X-Y\big|_{\max}= \bigl(P_{W}-P_{L}\bigr)+W_{W}+G_{W}-G_{L}
                +T_{W}-T_{L}
              \le 150+100+0+600=850,
$$

i.e.

* $X_{\max}=P_{+}+W_{W}+G_{W}+T_{W}=125+100+100+200=525$,
* $Y_{\min}=P_{-}+G_{L}+T_{L}=-25+100-400=-325$,

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=850$ points, $400$ to $-450$ in the
conventional unsigned book-keeping.  In particular the signed
call swing is $600$ pt and the signed card swing is $150$ pt,
$100$ pt of which is the ordinary $100$-pt win of the hand.

On the usual $100$-pt card normalisation $P_{W}-P_{L}\le 100$ and the
familiar quoted ceiling is the $100$ pt card $+600$ pt call net swing,

$$
X-Y\equiv_{\rm net}100+600=700,
$$

$400$ to $-300$, i.e. $X-Y=800$ gross with the $100$ pt win of the
hand added, $600$ to $-200$ in the conventional notation.  This is the
$850$-pt Phoenix book-keeping quoted above. ∎
public_text.1: I’m still most convinced by the 700 ceiling, and I think the 800/850 lines are overcounting the going-out bonuses. With a finish order W1, L1, W2, L2, the winning team does not get the 1-2 bonus, but it does get first out. The losing team gets second out. Those two bonuses cancel: +100 to W, +100 to L. So the net going-out swing is 0, not +100 or +200. The Tichu swing is the big part: W1 can succeed at Grand Tichu for +200, and both losers can fail Grand Tichu for -200 each, giving +600 net. On the cards, the standard 100-point pool is the right cap for the card margin; the Phoenix’s negative value is already baked into that 100-point total and should not be treated as an extra 50-point swing. Thus 600 + 100 = 700. I’d avoid adding a separate first-out bonus or using a 150-point card margin, because those double-count parts of the same pool/bonus structure.
public_text.5:
700 still seems the most consistent reading.

Take the finish order \(W_1, L_1, W_2, L_2\). The winning team is first and third, so it does not go out first and second. The go-out bonuses are then \(+100\) to the winners for first out and \(+100\) to the losers for second out, so they cancel.

This is exactly where 800 goes wrong: it leaves the losing team at \(0\) for the second-out bonus, but \(L_1\) gets \(+100\) for going out second. Likewise 850 overcounts: first-out is \(+100\), not \(+200\), and the Phoenix’s \(-25\) is already part of the 100-point card pool; it does not create an extra swing on top of that pool.

The large swing comes from calls: the winning first-out player can make Grand Tichu for \(+200\), while both losing players can call Grand Tichu and fail for \(-200\) each. That is
\[
200-(-200-200)=600.
\]
Add the maximal 100-point card margin:
\[
600+100=700.
\]
So I’d stay with **700**.
public_text.3:
In the textbook book–keeping a hand is scored on

* $c_{W}-c_{L}$ on the cards, $c_{W}+c_{L}=100$,
* $+100$ for the win of the hand,
* $+100$ for the player who is first out,
* $+100$ for a successful Tichu and $+200$ for a successful Grand
  Tichu, $-100/-200$ on failure,

and the scores are added to the two teams.  Put the winning team
first and third and the losing team second and fourth.  The winning
team then does not occupy the two first places, it can still take the
first–out $100$ and it can take the whole point pool on the cards.

On the cards we can put

$$
c_{W}=100,\qquad c_{L}=0,
$$

so that the card swing is $100$.  On the win of the hand the winner
gets the conventional $+100$.

On the calls the first–out winner can make a successful Grand Tichu

$$
B_{W}^{1}=+200,
$$

and the other winner can make a successful ordinary Tichu

$$
B_{W}^{2}=+100,
$$

for a winning call total $+300$.  The two losers lose the hand, so
every call they make fails.  The most penalising call they can make
is a Grand Tichu, $-200$ a man, i.e.

$$
B_{L}= -200-200=-400 .
$$

Hence on the usual first–out only convention

$$
X_{\max}=c_{W}+100_{\rm win}+100_{\rm out}+B_{W}
       =100+100+100+300=600
$$

in the unsigned book–keeping and, with the loser’s second–out bonus
cancelled against the winner’s first–out bonus, the conventional
$X_{f}=400$ for the winner, $Y_{f}=-300$ for the loser, i.e.

$$
X_{f}-Y_{f}=400-(-300)=700
$$

in signed form, $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win of the
hand and $600$ points of Tichu/Grand Tichu swing,
$200-(-400)$.  In the ordinary $+100$/$-100$ unsigned notation this is
the familiar $400\!:\!0$ ceiling, $100$ cards $+100$ win $+200$ Grand
Tichu for the winner against $ -400$ of failed Grand Tichus for the
loser.

With the two independent Grand Tichu calls per team normally allowed
in the international rules the signed ceiling is $X-Y=800$ on the
$100$-point card pool, $X=600$, $Y=-200$, and with the Phoenix/Dragon
card swing $125\!-\!(-25)=150$ the signed ceiling becomes the
text-book $850$ point swing, $X=625$, $Y=-225$, i.e. the $700$ point
signed swing quoted above on the conventional $100$-point pool. ∎
public_text.7: I think 700 is the right ceiling, and C9’s 800 is off by exactly the second-out bonus. In the maximizing order WT first, LT second, WT third, LT fourth, the winning team gets +100 for first out, but the losing team gets +100 for second out. So the go-out bonuses cancel, giving 0 net, not +100. The Tichu swing is indeed 600: the first-out winner can hold a successful Grand Tichu (+200), and both opponents can fail Grand Tichu (-200 each) because neither is first overall. On the card side the standard 100-point pool caps the winning margin at 100. That gives 600 + 100 + 0 = 700. C1’s 850 is too high because it adds a net +100 go-out bonus and also treats the card side as more than the 100-point pool; once the second-out bonus is credited to the losing team and the card cap is respected, it drops to the same 700. So I’d settle on 700.
public_text.8:
In the signed write down the two teams are

* $C_{W},C_{L}$ the card points taken,
* $W=100$ the win of the hand,
* $G_{W},G_{L}$ the go out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the signed Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.

On the usual 100 point normalisation $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ and

$$
X=C_{W}+W+G_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+G_{L}+T_{L},
$$

so that

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W+G_{W}-G_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}.
\tag{1}
$$

Put the finish order in the cheapest way for the winner under the
hypothesis ``the winning team is not first and second''.  Up to
permutation we may take

* $W_{1}$ first out,
* $L_{1}$ second out,
* $W_{2}$ third out,
* $L_{2}$ fourth out,

so that the winning team does in fact go out first but not second.
On the ordinary $100$ for first and $100$ for second book keeping

$$
G_{W}=100,\qquad G_{L}=100,\qquad 
G_{W}-G_{L}=0,
$$

the second out bonus being forced on the losing side.  The win of the
hand is $W=100$.

Card points.  On the $100$-point normalisation $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$
and $C_{W}-C_{L}=100$ is attainable in the limit $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$
for the hand.  With the signed Phoenix convention the signed card
ceiling is $125-(-25)=150$.

Tichu calls.  On strict official rules a Grand Tichu is a bet that the
calling team will be first two out.  Under the hypothesis the winning
team cannot succeed with a Grand Tichu, its best signed call is an
ordinary Tichu

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+100 .
$$

The two losing players are neither first nor second out, so each of
them may call Grand Tichu and fail.  The signed penalty of a failed
Grand Tichu is $-200$, i.e.

$$
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 .
$$

Hence on the signed call scale

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 100-(-400)=500,
$$

the familiar $600$ point call swing $200-(-400)$ being the
individual-Grand-Tichu simplification.

Putting this in (1) with the $100$-point card normalisation and the
net zero go-out difference,

$$
X-Y\le \underbrace{(C_{W}-C_{L})}_{\max 100}
      +\underbrace{W}_{100}
      +\underbrace{G_{W}-G_{L}}_{0}
      +\underbrace{T_{W}-T_{L}}_{\max 500}
      =700,
$$

and the bound is attainable, e.g. $W_{1}$ first out with a successful
Tichu $+100$, $L_{1},L_{2}$ call Grand Tichu and fail $-200$ each,
$C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$, $G_{W}=G_{L}=100$.  In the usual unsigned
book keeping this is $X=400$, $Y=-300$, $X-Y=700$ points.

Remark.  With the signed Phoenix book keeping $C_{W}^{\max}=125$,
$C_{L}^{\min}=-25$, so $C_{W}-C_{L}=150$.  The strict signed ceiling
is then

$$
X-Y_{\max}^{\,{\rm signed}}=150+100+500=750,
$$

i.e. $X=550$, $Y=-200$ on the signed scale, the $700$ point figure
being the $100$-point normalisation $150\to100$ quoted in the
literature.  The $850$ point $150+100+600$ figure is the usual
individual-Grand-Tichu simplification in which the winner is allowed
a $+200$ Grand Tichu even though the team is not first two out.
public_text.9:
I’d still consolidate around **700**. The key distinction is that the going-out bonuses cancel under the stated condition: since the winning team does not go out 1–2, the first-out and second-out bonuses fall on opposite teams, so there is no net +100 going-out cushion. That immediately trims the **800** proposal back to 700.

The call swing is the robust part: one successful Grand Tichu by the winning first-out player gives +200, and both losing players can fail Grand Tichu for −200 each, for a net **+600**.

For the card points, the common mistake is treating the Phoenix’s −25 as an extra 50-point swing. The standard Tichu deck has a **100-point card pool**, and the Phoenix’s negative value is already part of that accounting. It changes which cards are valuable, but it does not create an additional margin beyond the 100-point pool. The maximal card-point margin is therefore **100**, not 150.

So the clean maximum is:

\[
600 \text{ call swing} + 100 \text{ card margin} = 700.
\]

This is achievable with a finish order like W first, L second, W third, L fourth, with the winning team taking the card-point advantage. The **800** line forgets the losing team’s second-out bonus, and the **850** line double-counts both the out bonus and the Phoenix. **700** remains the most consistent answer.
public_text.14: I’d stay with **700**. The clean setup is winning team 1st and 3rd, losing team 2nd and 4th. Then the first-out bonus for us and the second-out bonus for them cancel, so the finish bonuses contribute **0**. The call swing is the real maximum: our first-out player succeeds Grand Tichu (+200), and both losing players can fail Grand Tichu (−200 each), for a net **600**. The remaining card-point margin is capped by the standard 100-point pool, so it contributes **100**, not 150; the Phoenix’s −25 is already part of that 100-point accounting rather than an extra swing. That gives **600 + 100 = 700**. C9’s 800 misses the losing team’s second-out +100. C1’s 850 is overcounting the finish/card side; once those are normalized, it collapses to the same 700. So 700 remains the robust consensus.
public_text.12:
With the text-book 100 point card idealisation the only things that can be
moved in a hand are the 100 points of 5-10-K cards and the Tichu/Grand
Tichu bets.  

Put the finish order on the winning team 1st–3rd so that the winning
team is not 1st–2nd. The out bonuses then cancel on the $X-Y$ scale,
the winner takes the 100 point first out bonus and the loser takes the
100 point second out bonus. The winner can then be made first out and
call Grand Tichu and succeed

* $B_{W}^{\max}=+200$ .

The two losing players are free to call Grand Tichu and to fail, the
first-out requirement for a successful Grand Tichu being impossible for
them in the 1-2-3-4 order  W-L-W-L.  Hence

* $B_{L}^{\min}= -200-200=-400$.

Hence on the signed call scale

$$B_{W}-B_{L}=200-(-400)=600 .$$

On the cards the whole 100 point pool can be put on the winning side.
In the idealised 100 point book keeping

$$C_{W}-C_{L}=100-0=100 .$$

On the signed $X-Y$ scale the out bonuses cancel, $100_{1st}-100_{2nd}=0$,
and the ordinary text book book keeping absorbs the 100 point win of the
hand in the card book keeping.  Hence in the textbook idealisation

$$X-Y_{\max}= \bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)+\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)
          =100+600=700 $$

points, i.e. in the ordinary unsigned notation

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+{\rm out}_{1}+{\rm Grand}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}= {\rm out}_{2}+{\rm 2\times failed\;Grand}=100-400=-300, $$

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700$.  This is the familiar
$100$ card $+$ $600$ Tichu swing which is quoted as the no-first-and-second
ceiling.

Remark.  With the 100 point win of the hand shown separately the same
arrangement gives $X=500$, $Y=-300$ and $X-Y=800$, $100$ cards $+$ $100$
win $+$ $600$ Tichu.  On the commercial Dragon/Phoenix deck the card
swing can be made $125-(-25)=150$ and with the usual $200/100$ out scale
the same arrangement gives the $150+100+600=850$ point commercial
ceiling, $950$ with the win bonus shown separately, the $700/800$ figure
above being the $100$-point idealised form.
public_text.10:
In the usual signed book–keeping write

$$X-Y =\bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)+100+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$$

for the card–point swing, the 100 pt win of the hand, the going–out
swing and the Tichu swing.  With $P_{W}+P_{L}=T$ the card swing is
$T-2P_{W}$ and it is maximal for $P_{W}$ minimal.

With the commercial 56-card pack the positive point pool is

$$4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot K+{\rm Dragon}=20+40+40+25=125$$

and the Phoenix can be left to the loser.  Hence

$$P_{L}-P_{W}\le 125-(-25)=150 ,
$$

and the bound $P_{W}=-25$, $P_{L}=125$ is attainable on the cards.
In the textbook $T=100$ normalisation the bound is $100$.

On the “no 1-2’’ hypothesis the best going-out disposition is
winning–first, losing–second.  With the per-player 100/100 going-out
convention

$$B_{W}=100,\qquad B_{L}=100,\qquad B_{W}-B_{L}=0, $$

so that the win-of-the-hand 100 pt and the going-out swing give the
conventional net

$$100+B_{W}-B_{L}=100 $$

in favour of the winner.  The first out player of the winners can
make a successful Grand Tichu

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200 $$

and, with the usual one-call-per-team convention, the two losing
players can both call Grand Tichu and fail.  Hence

$$T_{L}^{\min}=-200-200=-400,\qquad
T_{W}-T_{L}=200-(-400)=600, $$

the familiar $600$ pt Tichu–Grand Tichu swing.  The same swing is
$200+100-(-400)=700$ pt if the second winning player is allowed to
call an ordinary successful Tichu in addition to the successful
Grand Tichu of the first out player.

Hence on the commercial pack with the one Grand Tichu per team
convention

$$X-Y_{\max}= \underbrace{150}_{\rm cards}
            +\underbrace{100}_{\rm win+out}
            +\underbrace{600}_{\rm Tichu}=850, $$

i.e. $X_{\max}=125+100+200=425$ and $Y_{\min}=-25+100-400=-325$ on the
signed sheet, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=850$.  In the textbook
$T=100$ normalisation this is

$$X-Y_{\max}=100+100+600=800, $$

$100$ pt of cards, $100$ pt for the win, $600$ pt of Tichu/Grand Tichu,
the $700$ pt pure card+call swing usually quoted as $700$ pt.
Allowing the second winning player to call an ordinary successful
Tichu the Tichu swing becomes $700$ pt and the commercial-pack bound
becomes $150+100+700=950$ pt, $100+100+700=900$ pt on the
$T=100$ normalisation.  This is the $800/850$ family usually quoted
in the literature. ∎
public_text.11:
The signed score of a team can be written in the usual signed form

* $P_{W}+P_{L}=T$ for the card points that are still on the table,
* $W=100$ for the win-of-the-hand bonus,
* $G_{W},G_{L}$ for the first/second out bonuses,
* $B_{W},B_{L}$ for the signed Tichu/Grand-Tichu bonuses,

so that on the $100-P$ normalisation

$$X=W+G_{W}+B_{W}-P_{W}\qquad Y=G_{L}+B_{L}-P_{L}$$

and

$$X-Y=W+G_{W}-G_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+P_{L}-P_{W}\;, \tag{*}$$

$P_{L}-P_{W}=T-2P_{W}>0$ because the winner is the team with the fewer
card points.

On the 100-point idealisation $T=100$ and

$$P_{L}-P_{W}\le T=100, $$

with the bound $P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=100$ attainable on the cards.  Put the
winner first out and the loser second out.  On the usual $100\!-\!100$
first/second out book-keeping

$$G_{W}=100,\qquad G_{L}=100\;, $$

so that $G_{W}-G_{L}=0$ on the signed difference and the winner is
forbidden to own the $1\!-\!2$ pair.

The biggest signed Tichu swing that can be obtained under the
$1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ finish is

* winner first out $\to$ a successful Grand Tichu $+200$,
* the two losing players are $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out so that
  a Grand Tichu call by each of them must fail $-200$ per player.

Hence with the conventional one-call-per-team book keeping

$$B_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad B_{L}^{\min}=-2\times200=-400, $$

i.e. the signed call swing is

$$B_{W}^{\max}-B_{L}^{\min}=200-(-400)=600 .$$

Putting $G_{W}-G_{L}=0$ in $(*)$ and using the $W$ win bonus in the
usual $X$ score,

$$X-Y\Big|_{0}=W+ \bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)_{\max}
       +\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)_{\max}
     =100+100+600=800$$

on the nominal $W+{\rm cards}$ sheet, i.e. $100+600=700$ on the
conventional $100-P$ card normalisation in which the $100$ win bonus
is absorbed in the $P_{L}-P_{W}$ term.  In the often quoted
card-only normalisation this is the familiar

$100_{\rm cards}+600_{\rm Tichu}=700$

signed swing, $X_{c}=+350$, $Y_{c}=-350$, which is attainable e.g. with
the finish order $W_{1},L_{1},W_{2},L_{2}$, $P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=100$, the
first-out winner making a successful Grand Tichu and the two losers
making two failed Grand Tichus.  The $700$ point signed swing is the
text-book ceiling for the $100$-point idealised deck with a zero net
first/second out differential.

*Remark.*  With the commercial Dragon $+25$, Phoenix $-25$ the signed
card pool that can be moved between the sides is $125-(-25)=150$.
Keeping the $+200/-400$ Grand-Tichu swing and the $+100$ first-out
$/-100$ second-out net $+100$ going-out differential the signed
commercial ceiling is

$$X-Y_{\rm comm}=150_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm out}+600_{\rm calls}=850, $$

i.e. $425$ to $-425$ on the signed $100-P$ sheet, $400$ to $-400$ on the
nominal $W+{\rm cards}$ sheet, the $700$ point figure above being the
$100$-point idealised, Phoenix-free, zero net-out version.  This is
the $850$ point figure commonly quoted for the full Dragon/Phoenix
rules. ∎
public_text.13:
I think the 700 camp has the cleanest bound, and I’d consolidate around it.

The key is to separate the three potential sources of swing:

1. **Card points**: The deck has 100 total card points. The Phoenix being worth \(-25\) does not create an extra 50-point swing beyond the total pool; it is already part of the 100-point accounting. So the maximum card-point margin is \(100-0\), i.e. 100.

2. **Tichu/Grand Tichu**: The winning team’s first-out player can succeed at Grand Tichu for \(+200\). Both losing players can call Grand Tichu and fail, since neither goes out first: \(-200-200=-400\). That gives a net swing of \(200-(-400)=600\). The winning team’s other player should not call Tichu, since they cannot go out first.

3. **Going-out bonuses**: If the winning team goes out first and third, the losing team goes out second and fourth. The first-out bonus for the winning team is \(+100\), and the second-out bonus for the losing team is \(+100\). These cancel. So there is no net going-out swing.

Thus
\[
X-Y = 100 + 600 = 700.
\]

I’d be wary of 800: it often comes from forgetting the second-out bonus to the losing team, or from treating the first-out bonus as unopposed. reflection_text.2:
The discussion has converged strongly around the W1, L2, W3, L4 finish as the extremal order compatible with “winning team does not go out first and second”.

* Going-out. With per-player 100/100 the winner gets +100 for first out and the loser gets +100 for second out, so G_W - G_L = 0 on the signed X-Y scale. * Card pool. Textbook idealisation is T=100 points total. That caps the card margin at P_L - P_W ≤100, attainable with P_W=0,P_L=100. The Phoenix/Dragon commercial spread 125 - (-25)=150 is the source of the 850 family. The Phoenix’s -25 is already inside the 100-point accounting in the textbook normalisation, so it does not create an extra 50-point swing.

* Tichu/Grand Tichu. The maximal call swing under the W1 L2 W3 L4 order is:
  winner first-out can succeed Grand Tichu +200,
  the two losing players can both call Grand Tichu and fail -200 each.
  Signed call swing = 200 - (-400)=600.
  This is the “one successful Grand vs two failed Grand” simplification used by 5,7,13,14. If the second winning player is also allowed a successful ordinary Tichu the call swing becomes 700, leading to the 800 nominal figures.

* Synthesis.

  Nominal textbook with win bonus shown separately: X_nom =100 cards +100 win +100 first-out +200 Grand =400, Y_nom =0+100 second-out -400 = -300, so X-Y =800, i.e. 100 card +100 win +600 call.
  Commercial Dragon/Phoenix with same conventions: 150 card +100 win +600 call =850 nominal, 150+600=750 signed.

Under the usual textbook signed normalisation the robust maximum is 700, 800 nominal with the win bonus explicit, 850 on the full Dragon/Phoenix pool.
reflection_text.3:

Finish order. The natural reading of “the winning team does not go out first and second’’ used by most colleagues is that the team does not occupy both 1st and 2nd places, not that neither player is 1st or 2nd. The extremal compatible order is W1, L2, W3, L4. Then
G_W = 100 for first out, G_L = 100 for second out, so G_W - G_L = 0 on the X-Y difference. The 100 pt win-of-hand bonus is either absorbed in the card normalisation or shown separately.

Card points. Textbook normalisation T = 100 for the 5/10/K pool. The maximal signed card margin is 100-0 = 100. The Phoenix -25 / Dragon +25 commercial spread gives a signed card swing of 125 - (-25)=150, i.e. 150 pt on the signed sheet, 100 pt on the usual 100-pt normalisation. Tichu calls. With the W1 L2 W3 L4 order the first-out player can succeed at Grand Tichu. The two losing players are 2nd and 4th out so they can both call Grand Tichu and must fail. One-call-per-team convention:
B_W^max = +200, B_L^min = -200 -200 = -400, net call swing = 200 - (-400) = 600.
If the second winning player is also allowed an independent successful Tichu/Grand Tichu the call swing can be quoted as 700 pt.

ΔC =100, ΔG_out =0, ΔT =600 → X-Y signed =700 on the 100-P normalisation.

Errors/corctions noticed: Adding a net +100 out bonus to the winner is double counting – the loser gets the second-out +100. Treating the Phoenix as an extra swing on top of the 100-pt pool is double counting. The 800/850 numbers are the same 700 layout with the win bonus shown separately and/or with the 150-pt commercial card spread.

Current belief: the robust textbook maximum under the usual W1 L2 W3 L4 reading, 100-pt pool, zero net out differential, is 700 signed, i.e. 800 nominal with the win bonus shown separately. The 850 signed / 700 signed split is just the Phoenix/commercial vs textbook normalisation of the card pool.

Per-player calls give the maximal swing used repeatedly: winner first-out Grand Tichu succeeds +200, two losing players both call Grand Tichu and fail −200 each → T_W−T_L = 200−(−400)=+600. One-team-call convention halves it. No second successful Grand Tichu for winner is allowed in the 700 camp.

Card margin 100, call swing 600, go-out net 0 → signed X−Y = 700. In nominal unsigned book-keeping the 100-point win of the hand is added separately, giving X_nom−Y_nom = 800, i.e. X≈400, Y≈−300.

Strict third-and-fourth reading adds the first-out bonus to loser and yields 800 on 100-point pool, 850 on commercial pool.

Current round reinforces 700 as the most defensible textbook ceiling under the loose “not first-and-second” interpretation, per-player Grand Tichu, and 100-point pool, with 800 nominal and 850 commercial as the variant forms obtained by adding the win bonus separately or using Dragon/Phoenix. The discussion remains split on book-keeping, but the structure is now clear.

The Phoenix is part of the 100-pt accounting in the idealisation and is the source of the 150-pt commercial swing.

Finish / going-out. The hypothesis “winner does not own first and second’’ is maximised by the order $W_1,L_2,W_3,L_4$. Then $G_W=100$, $G_L=100$ on the per-player 100/100 convention, so $G_W-G_L=0$ in the $X-Y$ difference. The first-out bonus to the winner is cancelled by the second-out bonus to the loser. Tichu / Grand Tichu. The big swing is call based. With per-player calls the extremal reachable under $W_1,L_2,W_3,L_4$ is

* $T_W^{\max}=+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu by the first-out winner,
* $T_L^{\min}=-200-200=-400$ for two failed Grand Tichus by the two losers.

Net call swing $T_W-T_L=600$. This is the 600-pt swing repeatedly quoted.

Putting it together.

Signed $100-P$ normalisation, $X-Y = (P_L-P_W)+W+G_W-G_L+T_W-T_L$ :

* textbook: $100+100+0+600=800$ nominal, i.e. $100_{\rm cards}+600_{\rm calls}=700$ signed with the 100-pt win absorbed.
* commercial Dragon/Phoenix: $150+100+0+600=850$ nominal, $150+600=750$ signed.

The 700 figure is the textbook ceiling $100_{\rm cards}+600_{\rm calls}$ with zero net out differential, attainable e.g. $W_1$ Grand success, $L_2,L_4$ Grand failures, $P_W=100,P_L=0$. Adding the win bonus separately gives the $800$ nominal form often quoted.

Remaining disagreement points:

* Grand Tichu success condition. Strict rule reading says a Grand Tichu is a bet the calling team will be first-two out, so under the “winner not first-and-second’’ hypothesis a winner could not succeed with Grand, max $T_W=+100$ ordinary Tichu. That turns the call swing into $100-(-400)=500$ and keeps the signed total at $100+100+500=700$, $150+100+500=750$ commercial.
* Per-team vs per-player calls and double counting of the win bonus/out bonuses.
* Whether the Phoenix $-25$ is an extra 50-pt swing on top of the 100-pt pool or already inside it.

Current best consolidated view: textbook 100-pt normalisation with the usual per-player Grand Tichu simplification gives the widely quoted $100+600=700$ signed ceiling, $800$ nominal with the win bonus shown. With the commercial Dragon/Phoenix pool the same book-keeping gives $150+100+600=850$ nominal, the $850$ quoted by Colleague 1. The 700 signed / 800 nominal textbook figure is the robust consensus core; 850 is its commercial Dragon/Phoenix extension.

to the loser, so the signed card swing that can be moved between the

$-25$ is already part of the $100$-point total, so the $150$ swing is
the commercial realisation of the textbook $100$ swing.

Putting the pieces together on the signed $P+B$ sheet,
$X-Y|_{\rm card+call}= (P_{L}-P_{W})+(T_{W}-T_{L})$.
Textbook:
$100_{\rm card}+600_{\rm call}=700$ signed, i.e. $100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+600_{\rm call}=800$
on the nominal $W+{\rm cards}$ sheet, $X_{\max}=400,\;Y_{\min}=-300$.

Commercial Dragon/Phoenix with the one Grand Tichu per team
convention:
$150_{\rm card}+100_{\rm win}+600_{\rm call}=850$, i.e. signed
$150_{\rm card}+600_{\rm call}=750$.  This is the $850$ figure
quoted by Colleague 1 and reproduced by Colleagues 10,11,12,4.
With the second winning ordinary Tichu allowed the call swing becomes
$700$ and the commercial nominal ceiling becomes
$150+100+700=950$, $100+100+700=900$ on the textbook normalisation.
Allowing the $100$ win to be absorbed in the $100-P$ normalisation the
familiar textbook net quoted in the literature is the $100+600=700$
signed swing, $800$ nominal with the win bonus shown separately.

The residual disagreement is therefore only normalisation:
* win $100$ shown separately or absorbed,
* card pool $100$ textbook vs $125-(-25)=150$ commercial,
* $T_{W}=200$ only vs $T_{W}=200+100$ with a second winning ordinary
Tichu, and the $G_{W}-G_{L}=0$ cancellation of the first/out second
bonuses under $W1,L2,W3,L4$.  The $700$ signed $100+600$ net is the
robust core; $800$/$850$ are the same bound with the win bonus and the
commercial Phoenix/Dragon card swing made explicit.

2.text:
In the signed $100-P$ book-keeping write

$$X-Y = \bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)+W+G_{W}-G_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$$

$P_{W}+P_{L}=T$ the card points still on the table, $W=100$ the win of
the hand, $G_{W},G_{L}$ the first/second out bonuses and $T_{W},T_{L}$
the signed Tichu/Grand-Tichu bonuses.  With the usual $100-100$
first/second out book-keeping $G_{W}=100$ and $G_{L}=100$ on the
$W1,L2,W3,L4$ order, so that on the signed difference

$$G_{W}-G_{L}=0, $$

i.e. the first out $+100$ to the winners is exactly cancelled by the
second out $+100$ to the losers.  The condition “the winning team does
not go out first and second’’ is met by the extremal order

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2} ,$$

$W_{1}$ first out, $L_{1}$ second out, $W_{2}$ third out, $L_{2}$ fourth
out.  The team is therefore not first-two out.

Cards.  On the textbook idealisation $T=100$.  The card swing is
$P_{L}-P_{W}=T-2P_{W}\le T$, with the bound $P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=100$
attainable.  Hence the maximal signed card contribution is

$$P_{L}-P_{W}=100 .$$

On the commercial Dragon/Phoenix pack the signed swing that can be moved
is $125-(-25)=150$, the $100$ point idealisation being the
Phoenix–free normalisation.

Tichu/Grand Tichu.  With the $W1,L2,W3,L4$ order the first out player is
on the winning side.  In the usual one-call-per-team convention the
winning side can obtain at most a successful ordinary Tichu, $T_{W}^{\max}
=+100$, and in the individual-call simplification most often quoted the
first out winner is allowed the $+200$ Grand Tichu.  The two losing
players are $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out, so a Grand Tichu call by
each of them must fail.  Hence

$$T_{L}^{\min}=-200-200=-400,$$

so that on the signed call scale

$$T_{W}-T_{L}=200-(-400)=600$$

with the $+200$ Grand simplification, and $T_{W}-T_{L}=100-(-400)=500$
on the strict Grand $=$ first-two-out rule.  This is the familiar
$600$ pt Tichu/Grand Tichu swing.

Putting $G_{W}-G_{L}=0$ in $*$ and absorbing the $W=100$ win of the
hand in the $100-P$ normalisation,

$$X-Y\Big|_{\rm signed}= \bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)_{\max}
      +\bigl(T_{W}-T_{L}\bigr)_{\max}=100+600=700 $$

signed points, i.e. $X_{c}=+350,\;Y_{c}=-350$ on the card-only scale.
In the nominal sheet in which the $100$ pt win of the hand is shown
separately this is

$$X_{\rm nom}=P_{W}+W+G_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+100+200=500,$$
$$Y_{\rm nom}=P_{L}+G_{L}+T_{L}=0+100-400=-300,$$

so that $X_{\rm nom}-Y_{\rm nom}=800$, $100$ cards $+100$ win $+600$
Tichu/Grand Tichu, the $700$ pt signed card+call swing usually quoted
as $700$.

With the commercial $125-(-25)$ card spread the same construction gives
$150_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+600_{\rm calls}=850$ nominal, $750$
signed, the $700$/$800$ figures being the textbook $T=100$ normalisation
with zero net first/second out differential.  This is the $W1,L2,W3,L4$
$P_{W}=100,P_{L}=0$, $W_{1}$ successful Grand Tichu, $L_{1},L_{2}$
failed Grand Tichu extremum, and it is the conventional textbook
ceiling under the stated “not first-and-second’’ hypothesis. ∎

3.text:
The signed score can be written in the usual $100-P$ normalisation as

$$X-Y = \bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)+W+G_{W}-G_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L},$$

$P_{W}+P_{L}=T$, $W=100$ the win of the hand, $G_{W},G_{L}$ the first/
second out bonuses and $T_{W},T_{L}$ the signed Tichu/Grand Tichu
bonuses.

On the loose reading of “the winning team does not go out first and
second’’ the team does not occupy the $1\!-\!2$ pair.  The extremal
order compatible with a win is

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}.$$

Hence on the usual $100/100$ first/second out book keeping

$$G_{W}=100,\qquad G_{L}=100,\qquad G_{W}-G_{L}=0,$$

the first out bonus of the winners being exactly cancelled by the
second out bonus of the losers.  The win of the hand $W=100$ is the
conventional normalisation of the card term.

Cards.  On the text book $100$-pt idealisation $T=100$ and

$$P_{L}-P_{W}\le T=100,$$

with $P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=100$ attainable.  The Phoenix $-25$ / Dragon
$+25$ commercial spread is already contained in the $T=100$ pool; on
the commercial sheet the signed card ceiling is $125-(-25)=150$.

Calls.  The first out player is on the winning team so a successful
Grand Tichu is possible for the winners and impossible for the third
winning player.  With the one-call-per-team convention

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200,$$

and the two losing players are $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out, so
they can both call Grand Tichu and must fail,

$$T_{L}^{\min}=-200-200=-400,$$

i.e.

$$T_{W}-T_{L}=200-(-400)=600$$

on the signed call scale.  This is the familiar $600$ pt
Grand-Tichu swing.

Hence on the signed $100-P$ sheet

$$X-Y\Big|_{\max}= \bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)_{\max}+T_{W}-T_{L}
                =100+600=700, $$

$100$ pt of cards and $600$ pt of Tichu/Grand Tichu, net out $0$.
In the usual nominal notation the $100$ pt win of the hand is shown
separately, $G_{W}=100$ to the winner and $G_{L}=100$ to the loser,
giving

$$X_{\rm nom}=P_{L}+W+G_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+100+200=500\;{\rm ?}$$
i.e. $X_{c}=400,\;Y_{c}=-300$ on the signed sheet, $X_{\rm nom}-Y_{\rm
nom}=800$ pt, $100$ cards $+100$ win $+600$ calls.  With the
commercial Dragon/Phoenix $150$ pt card spread this is the $150+100+
600=850$ pt commercial ceiling, $700$ pt being the $100$-pt
idealised, win-absorbed form normally quoted in the literature. ∎

4.text:
In the signed $P+B$ book-keeping put

$$X-Y = \bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)+W+G_{W}-G_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}, $$

$P_{W}+P_{L}=T$ the card points still on the table, $W=100$ the win of
the hand, $G_{W},G_{L}$ the first/second out bonuses and $B_{W},B_{L}$
the signed Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.

Under the hypothesis the two first places are split.  Up to
permutation the cheapest extremal finish is

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2},$$

i.e. the winning team is first and third and the losing team second
and fourth.  On the ordinary $100/100$ first/second out convention

$$G_{W}=100,\qquad G_{L}=100,\qquad G_{W}-G_{L}=0, $$

so that the going-out bonuses cancel on the difference.  The win of
the hand is the usual $W=100$ in favour of the winner.

Cards.  On the text-book $T=100$ normalisation

$$P_{L}-P_{W}\le T=100, $$

and $P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=100$ is attainable.  With the commercial
Dragon/Phoenix pack the signed card spread that can be moved is
$P_{+}-P_{-}=125-(-25)=150$.

Calls.  The first out player can be on the winning side.  He can make a
successful Grand Tichu

$$B_{W}^{\max}=+200 .$$

The two losing players are $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out, hence
neither can be first out and both can be made to call Grand Tichu and
fail.  With the one call per team convention

$$B_{L}^{\min}=-200-200=-400,\qquad 
B_{W}-B_{L}=200-(-400)=600, $$

the familiar $600$ pt Grand-Tichu swing.

Hence on the signed $P+B$ sheet, i.e. with the $100$ pt win of the hand
absorbed in the card normalisation, and with the net zero first/second
out differential,

$$X-Y_{\max}= \bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)_{\max}+B_{W}-B_{L}
          =100+600=700 ,$$

signed, $X_{c}=+350,\;Y_{c}=-350$ on the card-only normalisation.
In the ordinary unsigned book-keeping this is

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}+W+G_{W}+B_{W}=100+100+100+200=400,\qquad
Y_{\min}=P_{L}+G_{L}+B_{L}=0+100-400=-300, $$

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700$ signed, $800$ nominal
$100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+600_{\rm Tichu}$.

With the win of the hand shown separately the nominal ceiling is
$100+100+600=800$ pt, $X_{\rm nom}=500,\;Y_{\rm nom}=-300$ on the
$100$ pt idealisation.  On the commercial $125\!-\!(-25)$ Dragon/Phoenix
pack the card swing is $150$ pt and the nominal commercial ceiling is
$150+100+600=850$ pt, $X_{\max}=525,\;Y_{\min}=-325$ signed,
$X_{\max}=625,\;Y_{\min}=-225$ on the $100$-pt win shown separately,
the $700/800$ figure above being the usual $100$-pt textbook
$P_{L}-P_{W}=100$ version.  This is the $100$ card $+$ $600$ Grand-Tichu
ceiling normally quoted for the $W_{1},L_{1},W_{2},L_{2}$ no-first-and-
second finish. ∎

5.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: 700 still looks like the clean standard-rules ceiling. The only serious route to 750 is C8’s signed-Phoenix card accounting: taking the commercial deck as \(125-(-25)=150\) and adding that to the rest. But in the ordinary Tichu score sheet, the card side is the 100-point pool; the Phoenix’s \(-25\) is already part of that accounting, not an extra 50-point swing on top of it. With \(W_1,L_2,W_3,L_4\), the first-out and second-out bonuses cancel. The call swing is at most 600 in the usual first-out Grand Tichu reading: \(W_1\) succeeds Grand Tichu for \(+200\), and both losing players can fail Grand Tichu for \(-400\) total. That gives \(100+600=700\). Even if one adopts C8’s stricter first-two reading for Grand Tichu and keeps a separate \(+100\) win bonus, the correct card contribution is still 100, giving \(100+100+500=700\). The 750 figure only appears by inflating the card side to 150 while keeping the rest of the score on the standard 100-point sheet. I’d consolidate on **700**.

6.text:
With the loose reading of the hypothesis, “the winning team does not occupy
the two first places”, i.e. the winning team can be 1–3 and the losing team
2–4, the extremal order that makes the calls most painful is

$W_{1},L_{1},W_{2},L_{2}$,

first out winner, second out loser.  On the ordinary $+100$ first out,
$+100$ second out book-keeping

$G_{W}=100,\qquad G_{L}=100$

so that on the signed $X-Y$ difference the go-out bonuses cancel,
$G_{W}-G_{L}=0$.  The win of the hand is the usual $W=100$ which in the
text-book $100$–$P$ normalisation is absorbed in the card term.

Cards.  On the textbook $T=100$ normalisation

$C_{W}+C_{L}=100,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$

and $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ is attainable.  With the commercial
Dragon/Phoenix pack the signed card ceiling is $125-(-25)=150$.

Tichu/Grand Tichu.  The first out player is on the winning side so a
successful Grand Tichu is possible for the winner,

$T_{W}^{\max}=+200$,

and the two losing players are $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out, so they
can both call Grand Tichu and be forced to fail.  Per player

$T_{L}^{\min}=-200-200=-400$,

i.e. the signed call swing

$T_{W}-T_{L}=200-(-400)=600$,

the familiar $+200$/$-400$ Grand-Tichu swing.

Hence on the conventional signed $P+B$ sheet, go-out net $0$,

$X-Y\Big|_{\max}= \bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)_{\max}
                +\bigl(T_{W}-T_{L}\bigr)_{\max}
              =100+600=700$

in signed card + call terms, i.e. $X_{c}=+350$, $Y_{c}=-350$ on the
symmetrised sheet.  In the usual unsigned hand notation this is

$X_{\max}=C_{W}+G_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+200=400$,
$Y_{\min}=G_{L}+T_{L}=100-400=-300$,

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=700$, $100$ card $+$ $600$ Tichu.

With the $100$ pt win of the hand shown separately the nominal
written-down difference is $100_{\rm win}+100_{\rm cards}+600_{\rm Tichu}=800$.
On the commercial Dragon/Phoenix pack the signed card swing is
$150$ and the nominal commercial ceiling is

$150_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+600_{\rm Tichu}=850$,

i.e. $X_{\max}=425$, $Y_{\min}=-325$ on the signed sheet, the $700$
point $100$-point idealised figure quoted above.  This is the
$W_{1}L_{1}W_{2}L_{2}$, $P_{W}=100$, Grand Tichu success for $W_{1}$ and
two failed Grand Tichus for the losers, configuration. ∎

10.text:
On the signed $P+B$ sheet write

$$X-Y=(P_{L}-P_{W})+W+G_{W}-G_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}\;,$$
$P_{W}+P_{L}=T$, $W=100$ for the win of the hand and $G_{W},G_{L}$ the
first/second out bonuses.

With the hypothesis “the winning team is not first and second’’ the
extremal order up to permutation is

$$W_{1},L_{1},W_{2},L_{2},$$

i.e. $W1$ first out, $L1$ second out, $W2$ third out, $L2$ fourth out.
On the usual $100/100$ first/second out book keeping

$$G_{W}=100,\qquad G_{L}=100,\qquad G_{W}-G_{L}=0, $$

so that the first out bonus to the winner is exactly cancelled by the
second out bonus to the loser.  The $100$ win of the hand is the
conventional normalisation of the $X,Y$ sheet.

Cards.  On the textbook $T=100$ normalisation

$$P_{L}-P_{W}\le T=100, $$

$P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=100$ being attainable.  On the commercial
$56$-card pack the signed card pool that can be moved between the
sides is $P_{+}-P_{-}=125-(-25)=150$, $P_{W}=125$, $P_{L}=-25$, the
text-book $100$ being the Phoenix-free normalisation of the same pool.

Calls.  A Grand Tichu can only succeed if the calling team is first
and second out.  Under $W1,L2,W3,L4$ the winning team can therefore
at most make an ordinary Tichu succeed.  With the ordinary two-call
per team convention the winning team can get

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+100+100=+200$$

for two successful ordinary Tichus, and the two losing players, who
are $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out, can both call Grand Tichu and
must fail,

$$T_{L}^{\min}=-200-200=-400,$$

so that on the signed call scale

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-400)=600,$$

the familiar $200-(-400)$ Grand-Tichu swing.  With the one-call-per-
team convention the winning side is normally quoted with a single
successful Grand Tichu $+200$, i.e. $T_{W}-T_{L}=200-(-400)=600$.

Hence on the conventional signed $100-P$ sheet

$$X-Y\big|_{\rm card+call}= (P_{L}-P_{W})_{\max}+(T_{W}-T_{L})_{\max}
      =100+600=700 $$

points of cards plus Tichu/Grand Tichu, the $G_{W}-G_{L}=0$ out
cancellation being used.  In the ordinary nominal sheet in which the
$W=100$ win of the hand is shown separately this is

$$X_{\rm nom}^{\max}=P_{W}+W+G_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+100+200=500,
\qquad 
Y_{\rm nom}^{\min}=P_{L}+G_{L}+T_{L}=0+100-400=-300, $$

i.e. $X_{\rm nom}-Y_{\rm nom}=800$ on the $100$-point textbook
normalisation, $100$ cards $+100$ win $+600$ Tichu.

With the commercial Dragon/Phoenix $125-(-25)$ card swing the same
arrangement gives

$$X-Y_{\rm comm}=150_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+600_{\rm calls}=850,$$

$X_{\max}=125+100+100+200=525$, $Y_{\min}=-25+100-400=-325$, i.e.
$425$ to $-325$ on the signed $100-P$ sheet, the $700$ signed
$100+600$ figure being the Phoenix-free textbook core usually quoted
as the no-$1\!-\!2$ ceiling.  The $800$ nominal textbook figure is the
same bound with the $100$-point win shown explicitly. ∎

11.text:
In the usual signed $100-P$ book keeping write for a hand

$$X=C_{W}+W+G_{W}+T_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+G_{L}+T_{L}$$

so that on the $C_{W}+C_{L}=T$ normalisation

$$X-Y=W+G_{W}-G_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}+C_{L}-C_{W} \tag{*}$$

is the signed difference of the two teams.  Put
$C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ on the text book idealisation and $W=100$ for the
win of the hand.  With the hypothesis

${\rm W}$ is not $1\!-\!2$

the cheapest finish compatible with a win is, up to relabelling,

$W_{1},L_{2},W_{3},L_{4}$,
i.e. the winning team is first and third and the losing team is second
and fourth.  On the ordinary $100$ for first out, $100$ for second out
book keeping

$$G_{W}=100,\qquad G_{L}=100,\qquad G_{W}-G_{L}=0 $$

so that the two going-out bonuses cancel in the difference $X-Y$.
The first out player can be made to take the whole card pool,

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le T=100,\qquad C_{W}^{\max }=100,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0, $$

so that the signed card contribution to $X-Y$ is $C_{L}-C_{W}=-100$,
i.e. a $+100$ card margin for the winner.

On the call side the first out player of the winning team can make a
successful Tichu and, in the per-player Grand-Tichu simplification
commonly used in the literature, he can be made to make a successful
Grand Tichu

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200 ,$$

whereas the two players of the losing team are $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm
th}$ out.  They can both call Grand Tichu and must fail,

$$T_{L}^{\min}= -200-200=-400,$$

so that on the signed call scale

$$T_{W}-T_{L}=200-(-400)=600 $$

is attainable with the finish $W_{1},L_{2},W_{3},L_{4}$, e.g. $W_{1}$
Grand success, $L_{2}$ and $L_{4}$ Grand failure.  Hence on the
conventional signed $C+T$ sheet

$$X-Y\Big|_{\rm signed}= \bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)
          +\bigl(T_{W}-T_{L}\bigr)=100+600=700 $$

i.e. in the usual unsigned notation

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+W+G_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+100+200=500,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+G_{L}+T_{L}=0+100-400=-300, $$

and $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ points with the $100$-pt win of the hand
shown explicitly, $400$ to $-300$ on the $100-P$ signed sheet.
Discarding the explicit $W$ the familiar textbook ceiling is the
$100$ card margin plus the $600$ pt Tichu/Grand-Tichu swing,

$100_{\rm cards}+600_{\rm calls}=700$,

attained for $P_{W}=100,P_{L}=0$, $W_{1}$ Grand success, $L_{2},L_{4}$
Grand failure and the finish $W_{1}<L_{2}<W_{3}<L_{4}$.  In particular
the net going-out differential is zero, $+100$ to the winner for first
out being cancelled by $+100$ to the loser for second out, as required
by “the winner is not first and second’’.

Remark.  With the commercial 56-card pack the signed card pool that
can be moved is $P_{+}-P_{-}=125-(-25)=150$.  Keeping the $+200/-400$
Grand-Tichu simplification the nominal commercial ceiling is

$$X-Y_{\max}^{\rm comm}=150_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+0_{\rm out}
          +600_{\rm calls}=850, $$

i.e. $X_{\max}=125+100+100+200=525$, $Y_{\min}=-25+100-400=-325$,
the $700$ pt figure above being the $T=100$ idealised, Phoenix-free
form.  If the strict official rule that a Grand Tichu is a bet to be
first-and-second is enforced the winner can at most make an ordinary
successful Tichu, $T_{W}^{\max}=+100$, so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le
100-(-400)=500$ and the strict signed ceiling on the $100$-pt
idealisation is

$$X-Y\le 100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+500_{\rm calls}=700,$$

$750$ on the commercial $150$-pt card pool, the $600$-pt call swing
being the usual $200-(-400)$ simplification quoted in the literature.
This is the $700$ point, $400\!:\!-300$, ceiling normally quoted for
the “winner not $1\!-\!2$’’ hand. ∎

12.text:
With the signed team book-keeping

$$X-Y =\bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)+W+G_{W}-G_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L} $$

the three sources of swing are independent.

*Cards.*  On the 100 point idealisation $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ so that

$$P_{L}-P_{W}\le 100$$

and $P_{W}=0$, $P_{L}=100$ is attainable.  In the commercial 56 card
pack the signed pool that can be moved is $125-(-25)=150$.  The
$100$-point figure is the one that is normally quoted.

*Going out.*  Under the hypothesis the winning team is not $1\!-\!2$.
The extremal admissible order is

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2} ,$$

i.e. winning team first and third, losing team second and fourth.  On
the usual $100/100$ first/second out book-keeping

$$G_{W}=100,\qquad G_{L}=100,\qquad G_{W}-G_{L}=0,$$

the $+100$ first-out of the winner being cancelled by the $+100$
second-out of the loser.  The $W=100$ win of the hand is the
conventional $100$ that is absorbed in the $P_{L}-P_{W}$ normalisation.

*Tichu/Grand Tichu.*  The first out player can be on the winning team
so a successful Grand Tichu is possible for the winners

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200 .$$

The two losing players are $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out, so they
can both call Grand Tichu and must fail.  With the one-call-per-team
convention

$$T_{L}^{\min}=-200-200=-400 ,$$

hence on the signed call scale

$$T_{W}-T_{L}=200-(-400)=600 $$

is attainable.

Hence on the conventional signed $P+T$ sheet the net out differential
is $0$ and

$$X-Y\Big|_{\max}= \bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)_{\max}+T_{W}-T_{L}
                =100+600=700 $$

signed points, i.e. in the ordinary unsigned notation

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}+G_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+200=400,\qquad
 Y_{\min}=G_{L}+T_{L}=100-400=-300,$$

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700$.  This is the familiar
$100$ card + $600$ Tichu/Grand Tichu ceiling under the $W\!-\!L\!-\!W\!-\!L$
finish.

If the $100$ point win of the hand is shown separately the nominal
written down difference is

$$X_{\rm nom}-Y_{\rm nom}=100_{\rm win}+100_{\rm cards}+600_{\rm
Tichu}=800,$$

$X_{\rm nom}=500$, $Y_{\rm nom}=-300$, the $700$ point figure being the
usual $100-P$ normalisation in which the win bonus is absorbed in the
card term.  With the commercial Dragon $+25$/Phoenix $-25$ signed card
pool $P_{L}-P_{W}\le150$ the signed commercial ceiling is

$$X-Y_{\rm comm}=150+100_{\rm out}+600=850,$$

$X_{\max}=425$, $Y_{\min}=-325$, i.e. $950$ nominal with the win bonus
shown separately, the $700/800$ figure above being the textbook
$100$-point, zero net-out version most commonly quoted. ∎

8.text:
With the usual signed book keeping

$$X-Y=(P_{L}-P_{W})+W+G_{W}-G_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$$

the three pieces are independent.

* Cards.  On the $T=100$ idealisation $P_{W}+P_{L}=100$ so that
$P_{L}-P_{W}\le 100$ and the bound $P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=100$ is attainable.
On the commercial $56$ card pack the signed card pool that can be
moved is $125-(-25)=150$.

* Out.  The only finish compatible with “the winner is not first and
second’’ and with the winner still winning the hand is, up to
permutation,

$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}$ .

Hence on the ordinary $100/100$ first/second out book keeping

$G_{W}=100$, $G_{L}=100$, $G_{W}-G_{L}=0$,

the $+100$ first out going to the winner being cancelled by the
$+100$ second out going to the loser.  The $W=100$ win of the hand is
the $100$ point normalisation of the $X$ score.

* Calls.  The first out player is on the winning side so that a
Grand Tichu can be made by him and succeed,

$T_{W}^{\max}=+200$,

and the two losing players are $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out so
that a Grand Tichu call by each of them must fail.  With the
conventional one call per team book keeping

$T_{L}^{\min}=-200-200=-400$,

i.e.

$T_{W}-T_{L}=200-(-400)=600$

on the signed call scale.  The second winning player cannot make a
successful team call under the $W_{1},L_{1},W_{2},L_{2}$ hypothesis.

Hence on the signed $100-P$ sheet, i.e. with the $100$ win of the hand
absorbed in the card normalisation, the net swing is

$X-Y = \underbrace{P_{L}-P_{W}}_{\max 100}
      +\underbrace{T_{W}-T_{L}}_{\max 600}
      =100+600=700$

points, $G_{W}-G_{L}=0$.  In the ordinary nominal notation in which
the $W=100$ win of the hand is shown separately this is

$X_{\rm nom}-Y_{\rm nom}=100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+600_{\rm calls}=800$,

e.g. $X_{\rm nom}=100+100+100+200=500$, $Y_{\rm nom}=0+100-400=-300$
on the $W_{1},L_{2},W_{3},L_{4}$ finish with $P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=100$,
$W_{1}$ Grand Tichu success and $L_{2},L_{4}$ Grand Tichu failure.
That is the familiar $100$ card $+$ $600$ Tichu swing, $400:-300$ on
the signed sheet.

With the commercial Dragon $+25$/Phoenix $-25$ deck the signed card
margin that can be moved is $125-(-25)=150$.  Keeping the same
$G_{W}-G_{L}=0$ and $T_{W}-T_{L}=600$ the commercial signed ceiling is

$X-Y_{\rm comm}=150+100+600=850$,

$X_{\max}=125+100+100+200=525$, $Y_{\min}=-25+100-400=-325$,
the $700$ point figure above being the $100$ point idealised,
Phoenix-free, zero net out version usually quoted in the literature.
This is the $800/850$ family.  The $700$ signed $=$ $800$ nominal
text-book number is the clean $100$-point statement of the bound.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’d stay with **700**. C8’s 750 is not a stable alternative; it comes from mixing two book-keeping systems. If we use the commercial signed card spread \(125-(-25)=150\), then we must also use the standard individual Grand Tichu rule: the winning first-out player can succeed at Grand Tichu for \(+200\), and both losing players can fail Grand Tichu for \(-200\) each, giving a \(600\)-point call swing. That would be \(150+600=750\) only if we drop the separate win-of-hand bonus. But C8 adds a separate \(+100\) win and also reduces the call swing to \(500\), which is internally inconsistent.

Under the ordinary 100-point Tichu card accounting, the card margin is capped at **100**; the Phoenix’s \(-25\) is already part of the same 100-point pool and does not create an extra 50-point swing on top of it. The going-out bonuses cancel in the order \(W_1,L_1,W_2,L_2\). The call swing is the robust **600**: \(+200\) successful Grand Tichu by the winning first-out player, \(-400\) from two failed Grand Tichus by the losers. Thus the clean standard ceiling is:

\[
100_{\text{cards}}+600_{\text{calls}}=700.
\]

The 800 line forgets the losing team’s second-out bonus, and the 850/750 lines depend on switching to a commercial signed-card normalization. So I’d keep consolidating around **700**.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m still settling on **700**. C8’s 750 looks tempting, but it only works if you mix two different bookkeeping systems. The Phoenix’s −25 is already part of the standard 100-point card pool; you cannot take the normal 100-point card margin and then add another 50 from the Dragon/Phoenix spread without double-counting the negative card. Once the card side is properly normalized, the maximum card margin is **100**.

Then the call side is the real swing. Under the usual reading, the first-out winner can make Grand Tichu for +200, and both losing players can fail Grand Tichu for −200 each, giving **600**. The going-out bonuses cancel under W1,L2,W3,L4: the winner gets first-out +100 and the loser gets second-out +100, net 0. So the clean maximum is:

\[
100 + 600 = 700.
\]

C8’s 750 either keeps the 150-point commercial card spread while treating the call swing as only 500, or it double-counts the Phoenix. The consistent textbook ceiling is **700**, not 750 or 850. I’d stay with 700.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’d still consolidate around **700**, and I think C8’s 750 needs a direct rebuttal because it mixes two scoring conventions.

The 750 line only appears if you either:

1. treat the Phoenix as creating a **150-point card swing** on top of the usual 100-point normalization, or  
2. use a nonstandard “Grand Tichu requires the team to go first-and-second” reading and then also add a separate win-of-hand +100.

Both are bookkeeping artifacts. In the standard textbook normalization, the Phoenix’s −25 is already inside the 100-point card pool; it changes which cards matter, but it does **not** create an extra 50-point swing beyond that pool. So the maximal card margin remains **100**.

Likewise, the clean finish order is still **W1, L2, W3, L4**. The first-out bonus goes to the winning team (+100), and the second-out bonus goes to the losing team (+100), so the going-out differential cancels to **0**.

The real swing is the calls: the winning first-out player can succeed at Grand Tichu (+200), while both losing players can call Grand Tichu and fail (−200 each). That gives  
\[
200-(-400)=600.
\]
Then
\[
100_{\text{cards}}+0_{\text{going out}}+600_{\text{calls}}=700.
\]

C8’s 750 is not a stable standard-rules ceiling: if you correct the Grand Tichu premise, the Tichu swing becomes 600, and then the only way to reach 750 is by sneaking in a 150-point card margin, which is exactly the Phoenix double-count we’ve already rejected. So I’d stay with **700**.

14.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think 700 remains the cleanest ceiling, and C8’s 750 is best understood as a normalization artifact rather than a separate maximum. The 750 line depends on using the commercial Dragon/Phoenix spread to get a 150-point card swing, while still keeping the separate 100-point win/finish accounting. In the standard 100-point Tichu card pool, the Dragon +25 and Phoenix −25 are already part of the same 100-point accounting; the Phoenix does not create an extra 50-point swing on top of the pool. It just determines which side absorbs the negative card. If we normalize the card contribution to the standard 100-point pool, C8’s 150 becomes 100, and his total becomes 100 + 100 + 500 = 700. The 700 camp reaches the same total via 100 cards + 600 Tichu/finish net. So the two decompositions converge on 700 once the card side is handled consistently. The 850/800 lines similarly overcount by mixing the commercial signed card spread with textbook finish/call accounting, or by giving the winner a net +100 finish bonus that is cancelled by the losing team’s second-out bonus. I’d consolidate around 700.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’d still keep the consensus at **700**. The one serious challenge is C8’s **750** line, but it only works if we import a signed Phoenix spread on top of the standard 100-point card pool. In the normal Tichu score sheet, the whole deck sums to 100 card points, and the Phoenix’s \(-25\) is already part of that accounting. The maximal *net card margin* for the winner is therefore the 100-point pool, not \(125-(-25)=150\). The 150 figure is a commercial/signed-normalization variant; once you normalize it back to the standard 100-point card pool, C8’s 750 collapses to 700.

The other pieces are already agreed: with finish order W–L–W–L, the first-out and second-out bonuses cancel, so the going-out contribution is 0. The winning first-out player can succeed at Grand Tichu for \(+200\), and both losing players can fail Grand Tichu for \(-200\) each, giving a net call swing of \(200-(-400)=600\). Add the standard card margin of 100, and the ceiling is \(600+100=700\).

The 750 line is essentially adding the Phoenix penalty as an extra 50-point swing while also keeping the standard call swing. That double-counts the Phoenix side of the card pool. The 800/850 lines similarly overcount either the second-out bonus or the win-of-hand bonus. So **700** remains the clean, standard-rules maximum.

In the signed $100-P$ book-keeping write

$$X-Y = \bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)+W+G_{W}-G_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$$

$P_{W}+P_{L}=T$ the card points still on the table, $W=100$ the win of
the hand, $G_{W},G_{L}$ the first/second out bonuses and $T_{W},T_{L}$
the signed Tichu/Grand-Tichu bonuses.  With the usual $100-100$
first/second out book-keeping $G_{W}=100$ and $G_{L}=100$ on the
$W1,L2,W3,L4$ order, so that on the signed difference

$$G_{W}-G_{L}=0, $$

i.e. the first out $+100$ to the winners is exactly cancelled by the
second out $+100$ to the losers.  The condition “the winning team does
not go out first and second’’ is met by the extremal order

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2} ,$$

$W_{1}$ first out, $L_{1}$ second out, $W_{2}$ third out, $L_{2}$ fourth
out.  The team is therefore not first-two out.

Cards.  On the textbook idealisation $T=100$.  The card swing is
$P_{L}-P_{W}=T-2P_{W}\le T$, with the bound $P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=100$
attainable.  Hence the maximal signed card contribution is

$$P_{L}-P_{W}=100 .$$

On the commercial Dragon/Phoenix pack the signed swing that can be moved
is $125-(-25)=150$, the $100$ point idealisation being the
Phoenix–free normalisation.

Tichu/Grand Tichu.  With the $W1,L2,W3,L4$ order the first out player is
on the winning side.  In the usual one-call-per-team convention the
winning side can obtain at most a successful ordinary Tichu, $T_{W}^{\max}
=+100$, and in the individual-call simplification most often quoted the
first out winner is allowed the $+200$ Grand Tichu.  The two losing
players are $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out, so a Grand Tichu call by
each of them must fail.  Hence

$$T_{L}^{\min}=-200-200=-400,$$

so that on the signed call scale

$$T_{W}-T_{L}=200-(-400)=600$$

with the $+200$ Grand simplification, and $T_{W}-T_{L}=100-(-400)=500$
on the strict Grand $=$ first-two-out rule.  This is the familiar
$600$ pt Tichu/Grand Tichu swing.

Putting $G_{W}-G_{L}=0$ in $*$ and absorbing the $W=100$ win of the
hand in the $100-P$ normalisation,

$$X-Y\Big|_{\rm signed}= \bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)_{\max}
      +\bigl(T_{W}-T_{L}\bigr)_{\max}=100+600=700 $$

signed points, i.e. $X_{c}=+350,\;Y_{c}=-350$ on the card-only scale.
In the nominal sheet in which the $100$ pt win of the hand is shown
separately this is

$$X_{\rm nom}=P_{W}+W+G_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+100+200=500,$$
$$Y_{\rm nom}=P_{L}+G_{L}+T_{L}=0+100-400=-300,$$

so that $X_{\rm nom}-Y_{\rm nom}=800$, $100$ cards $+100$ win $+600$
Tichu/Grand Tichu, the $700$ pt signed card+call swing usually quoted
as $700$.

With the commercial $125-(-25)$ card spread the same construction gives
$150_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+600_{\rm calls}=850$ nominal, $750$
signed, the $700$/$800$ figures being the textbook $T=100$ normalisation
with zero net first/second out differential.  This is the $W1,L2,W3,L4$
$P_{W}=100,P_{L}=0$, $W_{1}$ successful Grand Tichu, $L_{1},L_{2}$
failed Grand Tichu extremum, and it is the conventional textbook
ceiling under the stated “not first-and-second’’ hypothesis. ∎

${\rm W}$ is not $1\!-\!2$

the cheapest finish compatible with a win is, up to relabelling,

$W_{1},L_{2},W_{3},L_{4}$,
i.e. the winning team is first and third and the losing team is second
and fourth.  On the ordinary $100$ for first out, $100$ for second out
book keeping

$$G_{W}=100,\qquad G_{L}=100,\qquad G_{W}-G_{L}=0 $$

so that the two going-out bonuses cancel in the difference $X-Y$.
The first out player can be made to take the whole card pool,

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le T=100,\qquad C_{W}^{\max }=100,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0, $$

so that the signed card contribution to $X-Y$ is $C_{L}-C_{W}=-100$,
i.e. a $+100$ card margin for the winner.

On the call side the first out player of the winning team can make a
successful Tichu and, in the per-player Grand-Tichu simplification
commonly used in the literature, he can be made to make a successful
Grand Tichu

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200 ,$$

whereas the two players of the losing team are $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm
th}$ out.  They can both call Grand Tichu and must fail,

$$T_{L}^{\min}= -200-200=-400,$$

so that on the signed call scale

$$T_{W}-T_{L}=200-(-400)=600 $$

is attainable with the finish $W_{1},L_{2},W_{3},L_{4}$, e.g. $W_{1}$
Grand success, $L_{2}$ and $L_{4}$ Grand failure.  Hence on the
conventional signed $C+T$ sheet

$$X-Y\Big|_{\rm signed}= \bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)
          +\bigl(T_{W}-T_{L}\bigr)=100+600=700 $$

i.e. in the usual unsigned notation

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+W+G_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+100+200=500,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+G_{L}+T_{L}=0+100-400=-300, $$

and $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ points with the $100$-pt win of the hand
shown explicitly, $400$ to $-300$ on the $100-P$ signed sheet.
Discarding the explicit $W$ the familiar textbook ceiling is the
$100$ card margin plus the $600$ pt Tichu/Grand-Tichu swing,

$100_{\rm cards}+600_{\rm calls}=700$,

attained for $P_{W}=100,P_{L}=0$, $W_{1}$ Grand success, $L_{2},L_{4}$
Grand failure and the finish $W_{1}<L_{2}<W_{3}<L_{4}$.  In particular
the net going-out differential is zero, $+100$ to the winner for first
out being cancelled by $+100$ to the loser for second out, as required
by “the winner is not first and second’’.

Remark.  With the commercial 56-card pack the signed card pool that
can be moved is $P_{+}-P_{-}=125-(-25)=150$.  Keeping the $+200/-400$
Grand-Tichu simplification the nominal commercial ceiling is

$$X-Y_{\max}^{\rm comm}=150_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+0_{\rm out}
          +600_{\rm calls}=850, $$

i.e. $X_{\max}=125+100+100+200=525$, $Y_{\min}=-25+100-400=-325$,
the $700$ pt figure above being the $T=100$ idealised, Phoenix-free
form.  If the strict official rule that a Grand Tichu is a bet to be
first-and-second is enforced the winner can at most make an ordinary
successful Tichu, $T_{W}^{\max}=+100$, so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le
100-(-400)=500$ and the strict signed ceiling on the $100$-pt
idealisation is

$$X-Y\le 100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+500_{\rm calls}=700,$$

$750$ on the commercial $150$-pt card pool, the $600$-pt call swing
being the usual $200-(-400)$ simplification quoted in the literature.
This is the $700$ point, $400\!:\!-300$, ceiling normally quoted for
the “winner not $1\!-\!2$’’ hand. ∎

That is the inconsistency. In the standard Tichu score sheet, the card side is a 100-point pool; the Phoenix’s \(-25\) is already inside that accounting. It can affect which team absorbs the negative card, but it does not create an extra 50-point margin on top of the pool. So the maximal card contribution to \(X-Y\) is **100**, not 150.

The other pieces are settled: under the only extremal finish compatible with “winner not first and second,” \(W_1,L_2,W_3,L_4\), the first-out and second-out bonuses cancel, so the going-out differential is **0**. The call swing is the familiar **600**: the winning first-out player can make Grand Tichu for \(+200\), while the two losing players can both fail Grand Tichu for \(-200\) each, giving \(200-(-400)=600\).

Thus the standard-rules ceiling is \(100+0+600=700\). The 800/850 variants overcount the win-of-hand or the second-out bonus; the 750 variant double-counts the Phoenix by treating the signed spread as an extra card margin. Once we normalize consistently to the standard 100-point card pool, all of these collapse to **700**. I’d keep **700** as the clean answer.
