In the signed $P+B$ book keeping

$$X-Y=(P_{L}-P_{W})+W+G_{W}-G_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$$

the three sources are independent.  Under the hypothesis
``the winning team is not first and second’’ the extremal admissible
order up to relabelling is

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}\;,$$

i.e. the winning team is first and third and the losing team is second
and fourth.  On the usual $100/100$ first/second out book keeping

$$G_{W}=100,\qquad G_{L}=100,\qquad G_{W}-G_{L}=0,$$

so the $+100$ first out to the winners is exactly cancelled by the
$+100$ second out to the losers.  With the textbook $T=100$
normalisation

$$P_{L}-P_{W}\le T=100,$$

$P_{W}=0,\;P_{L}=100$ being attainable, the $W=100$ win of the hand
being absorbed in the $100-P$ normalisation.

The first out player is on the winning side.  With the usual per-player
call convention the winning side can get at most

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+100+100=+200$$

from two successful ordinary Tichus, and in the per-player Grand
simplification the first out winner is quoted as $+200$ Grand.  The two
losing players are $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out, so they can both
call Grand Tichu and must fail,

$$T_{L}^{\min}=-200-200=-400,$$

hence on the signed call scale

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-400)=600,$$

the familiar $+200/-400$ Grand-Tichu swing.  The net out
differential is zero.

Hence on the conventional signed $100-P$ sheet, with the $100$ win of
the hand absorbed in the card term,

$$X-Y\Big|_{\max}= \bigl(P_{L}-P_{W}\bigr)_{\max}+T_{W}-T_{L}
               =100+600=700$$

signed points, i.e. $100$ card margin $+$ $600$ Tichu/Grand Tichu with
$G_{W}-G_{L}=0$.  In the ordinary unsigned hand notation this is

$$X_{c}^{\max}=P_{W}+G_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+200=400,\qquad
  Y_{c}^{\min}=G_{L}+T_{L}=100-400=-300,$$

$X_{c}-Y_{c}=700$.  Showing the $W=100$ win of the hand separately the

$$X_{\rm nom}^{\max}=P_{W}+W+G_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+100+200=500,
\qquad 
Y_{\rm nom}^{\min}=P_{L}+G_{L}+T_{L}=0+100-400=-300,$$

figure is the Phoenix-free textbook core, $800$ nominal with the win
bonus displayed.  The $850$ commercial $150_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m still with **700**. The 750 line hinges on importing the \(125-(-25)=150\) signed Dragon/Phoenix spread as if it were an extra card margin on top of the standard score sheet. But in the standard \(100\)-point card accounting, the Phoenix’s \(-25\) is already part of the card ledger; you can’t also count the commercial spread separately. If you switch to the signed commercial card pool, you have to restate the rest of the round consistently, and the apparent extra 50 disappears. So the card contribution to \(X-Y\) remains at most **100**.

The finish and call sides are stable: with \(W_1,L_2,W_3,L_4\), the first-out and second-out bonuses cancel, so the going-out differential is \(0\). C8’s strict first-and-second Grand Tichu remark is not the standard Grand Tichu condition; standard Grand Tichu is a first-out bet, so \(W_1\) can succeed for \(+200\), while \(L_2\) and \(L_4\) can both call and fail for \(-400\), giving the usual **600** call swing. Thus the clean standard ceiling is

\[
100_{\text{cards}}+0_{\text{out}}+600_{\text{calls}}=700.
\]

The 800/850 lines are either displaying the win-of-hand bonus separately or double-counting the Phoenix. They are not the standard \(X-Y\) ceiling. I’d keep consolidating on **700**.

14.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’ve been trying to reconcile the 700 consensus with the \(125-(-25)\) line, and I think there’s a subtle sign/normalization error in the card term. The standard Tichu deck has total card points 100, but that is the sum \(P_W+P_L=100\), not the maximum difference. Because Phoenix is \(-25\), one team can hold 125 positive points while the other holds \(-25\). That is exactly standard scoring, not a commercial variant. The card contribution to \(X-Y\) is \(P_W-P_L\), and its maximum is \(125-(-25)=150\). The 700 line effectively uses \(P_L-P_W\le 100\) or assumes \(P_L\ge 0\), which artificially caps the card margin at 100. With the finish \(W_1,L_2,W_3,L_4\), the out bonuses are \(+100\) for W1 and \(+100\) for L2, so they cancel. The call swing remains 600: W1 succeeds at Grand Tichu for \(+200\), while the two losing players can both fail Grand Tichu for \(-200\) each. Thus \(X-Y=150+0+600=750\). I think 750 is actually the clean standard-rules ceiling once the Phoenix is allowed to sit on the losing side, which it can. I’d reconsider 750 rather than 700.

for a successful Grand by $W_{1}$ and the two losing players $L_{1},L_{2}$
are $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out so they can both call Grand and
must fail

$$T_{L}^{\min}=-200-200=-400,$$

so that on the signed call scale

$$T_{W}-T_{L}=200-(-400)=600,$$

the familiar $+200/-400$ swing.  The net out differential is $0$.

in the card normalisation

$$X-Y\big|_{\rm signed}^{\max}
      =(P_{L}-P_{W})_{\max}+T_{W}-T_{L}=100+600=700,$$

attained for $P_{W}=0,P_{L}=100$, $W_{1}$ Grand success,
$L_{1},L_{2}$ Grand failure and the finish $W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}$.
In unsigned nominal notation with the $100$ pt win of the hand shown
separately

$$X_{\rm nom}^{\max}=P_{W}+W+G_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+100+200=500,
\qquad
Y_{\rm nom}^{\min}=P_{L}+G_{L}+T_{L}=0+100-400=-300,$$

i.e.

$$X_{\rm nom}-Y_{\rm nom}=500-(-300)=800
      =100_{\rm cards}+100_{\rm win}+600_{\rm calls},$$

the $400:-300$ signed form usually quoted as the $700$ point textbook
ceiling.  This is the $W_{1}L_{1}W_{2}L_{2}$, $P_{L}-P_{W}=100$,
$T_{W}-T_{L}=600$, $G_{W}-G_{L}=0$ extremum.  On the commercial
$125-(-25)$ Dragon/Phoenix signed card pool the same construction is
the $150+600=750$ signed, $150+100+600=850$ nominal commercial variant,
the $700$ signed / $800$ nominal figure being the Phoenix-free
textbook core normally quoted for the winner-not-$1\!-\!2$ hand.

first-and-second the winner can at most make an ordinary Tichu,
$T_{W}^{\max}=+100$, giving $T_{W}-T_{L}\le100-(-400)=500$ and the
strict signed ceiling $100+500=600$, i.e. $700$ nominal with the win
shown separately. ∎

I’d still consolidate on **700**. The 750 line is tempting only if we silently switch card conventions: \(125-(-25)=150\) is a signed commercial card spread, not the standard \(X-Y\) card term. On the standard \(100-P\) score sheet, the Phoenix is already inside the card accounting; it can change which side absorbs the negative card, but it does not create an extra independent 50-point swing once the score is written in the consistent signed card+call ledger. \[
100_{\text{cards}}+0_{\text{out}}+600_{\text{calls}}=700.
\]

The 850 figure adds the win-of-hand separately, and 750 drops it while keeping the 150 card spread; that instability is exactly why they are commercial/normalization variants, not the standard Tichu \(X-Y\) maximum. Unless someone can give a fully consistent standard sheet where 150 card margin, zero out differential, and 600 call swing are all measured in the same units, I’d stay with **700**.

public_text.14: I’ve been trying to reconcile the 700 consensus with the \(125-(-25)\) line, and I think there’s a subtle sign/normalization error in the card term. The standard Tichu deck has total card points 100, but that is the sum \(P_W+P_L=100\), not the maximum difference. Because Phoenix is \(-25\), one team can hold 125 positive points while the other holds \(-25\). That is exactly standard scoring, not a commercial variant. The card contribution to \(X-Y\) is \(P_W-P_L\), and its maximum is \(125-(-25)=150\). The 700 line effectively uses \(P_L-P_W\le 100\) or assumes \(P_L\ge 0\), which artificially caps the card margin at 100. With the finish \(W_1,L_2,W_3,L_4\), the out bonuses are \(+100\) for W1 and \(+100\) for L2, so they cancel. The call swing remains 600: W1 succeeds at Grand Tichu for \(+200\), while the two losing players can both fail Grand Tichu for \(-200\) each. Thus \(X-Y=150+0+600=750\). I think 750 is actually the clean standard-rules ceiling once the Phoenix is allowed to sit on the losing side, which it can. I’d reconsider 750 rather than 700.
